headline: Medium-risk pair: shared broad egress and overlapping file/API surfaces create leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between chatwoot and RD-Agent, so a prompt-injection bridge is not proven. However, chatwoot can ingest messages and RD-Agent can run browsers and call APIs, so a manual copy/paste or exported-content bridge is plausible. Uncertainty keeps this above none, but below medium because the shared path is not default.
conditions: IF chatwoot outputs are manually copied into RD-Agent prompts or browser inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of untrusted chat transcripts into RD-Agent prompts.
Add a short prompt prefix that treats imported text as data, not instructions.
Use a separate staging channel for any chatwoot exports.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before RD-Agent ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while RD-Agent touches logs and execution traces and has broad network egress plus API keys. A shared workspace is not documented, but both agents can move data outward through APIs or logs, so leakage is plausible in default deployments. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF customer data from chatwoot is forwarded into RD-Agent logs or prompts, leakage occurs.
IF RD-Agent is configured to send logs or traces to external services, sensitive chatwoot content may exit the boundary.
mitigations: Remove customer identifiers from any data passed to RD-Agent.
Rotate and scope RD-Agent API keys to non-production where possible.
Review log destinations and disable verbose logging for shared runs.
Use a separate export folder for chatwoot artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate network and storage boundaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly supports multiple instances and writes to log/, while chatwoot is a runnable open-source service with broad network egress and API integrations. A shared writable directory is not documented, so I cannot claim a direct lock conflict; uncertainty escalates to medium because overlapping mutable surfaces are plausible and the pair could contend over shared files or external resources if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem path, write conflicts become possible.
IF both agents mutate the same external API-backed resource, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories to each agent.
Avoid sharing the same API credentials across both agents.
Run one agent at a time when modifying the same external resource.
Check for existing lockfiles before starting a job.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking for shared mutable targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a research/automation system that can act on outputs, and chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports. If chatwoot content is fed into RD-Agent without verification, RD-Agent may amplify errors into downstream actions or reports. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities rather than directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF chatwoot outputs are used as authoritative inputs to RD-Agent workflows, errors can cascade.
IF RD-Agent generates reports or actions from unverified chatwoot text, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before RD-Agent acts on chatwoot-derived content.
Mark chatwoot exports as untrusted input in prompts.
Add a verification checklist for any generated report.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis for chatwoot-derived tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and interaction history, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, logs, and execution traces and uses third-party APIs. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so I cannot claim high severity; however, the pair creates a plausible compliance gap if regulated customer data is routed into RD-Agent's external API workflow or logs.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from chatwoot is sent into RD-Agent's external API calls, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention policies differ between chatwoot records and RD-Agent logs, deletion/export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated customer data into RD-Agent prompts or logs.
Confirm retention settings for both systems before shared use.
Document which data classes may cross the boundary.
Purge test runs containing customer data.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and DPA controls across both systems.
